page.layout: One column of text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top. Division heads "EXERCITATIO II." and "CAP. I." centred, with subtitles below them. Page number at top right. Catchword "Dei" at bottom right, signature "Q 3" at bottom centre.

main_text.p: voluntates ad omnes actus suos? Sed quaero, an sit certitudo actuum liberorum futurorum antecedenter ad decreta Dei? Si sit, tum etiam est necessitas fundamentalis & entitativa in iis antecedenter ad Dei decreta: Erg. Deus non habet in sua potestate aliter decernere actus liberos, quam sunt antecedenter ad Dei decreta. Eligat jam Iesuita utrum Deum, an homines velit necessitari ad actus liberos. 2. Videtur sequi hinc duas esse necessitates actuum liberorum, unam antecedenter, aliam consequenter ad Dei decreta: at quid opus est Deus praescire in actu approbativo & permissivo futuros actus liberos, si jam sunt illi actus Deo certissimi ante omnes Dei voluntatis approbativos & permissivos actus? Sed nos Arrianis primis hujus scientiae authoribus, ut observat Did. Alvarez, & novatoribus hisce relinquamus hoc mysterium pudendum.
main_text.head: EXERCITATIO II.
De notionibus divinae voluntatis.
CAP. I.
main_text.p: AGnoscunt unanimiter Scholastici hanc di-Bannes tom. 1. q. 19. art. 6. stinctionem: circa objectum ipsius non nihil discrepant. D. Bannes ait, probabile esse Alexan. 1. quod fit in Deo formaliter actus volendi bonum, qui non compleatur. Alexander Halensis, Cajetanus, Driedo, & alii agnoscunt non esse Deip. q. 36. art. 2.Cajet. in. 1.Tim. 2.Driedo de concl. 1.q. p. 4.
[?] Note marks and references are printed in the margin; see the notes below.

page.notes: The right margin carries the references: "Bannes tom. 1. q. 19. art. 6", "Alexan. 1.", "p. q. 36. art. 2", "Cajet. in. 1.", "Tim. 2.", "Driedo de conc. 1." and "q. p. 4." Several are abbreviated and uncertain, so the exact wording is marked where it is doubtful. The first word "AGnoscunt" starts with a large initial A. The word "distinctionem" is broken as "di-" / "stinctionem": the first letter of the second line is an ornamental form and is read as s. The title "Cap. I." and its subtitle are set in centred type. The short line "Eligat jam Iesuita utrum Deum, an homines" carries a small mark after "homines" that may be a printing sign; it is left as "homines". The paragraph beginning "voluntates" continues from the previous page.
